<!-- pr-reviewer: eedc5754aea284bdf4cebe5c40cfc5d9370d6ee3 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

SAFETY-tier review. No blocking findings.

The three posts refuse positive G73 and G85 dwell before cycle output or a modal X/Y continuation. Zero-dwell output stays unchanged. The tests cover later holes and raw sub-millisecond dwell. The new test file uses the correct crate and has a provenance statement.

Local verification used `.claude/worktrees/review-2654`, trial-merged with upstream/main at `136f19763e791b397eb7b2609247230ac1007363`. The merge had no conflicts. No GitHub runner was used.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `bore_cycle`: 9 passed.
- `cycle_dwell`: 9 passed.
- `cycle_hop`: 7 passed.
- `dwell_cycles_modal_p`: 5 passed.
- `g73_g85_dwell_linuxcnc`: 7 passed.
- `g83_dwell_linuxcnc`: 2 passed.
- `ream_cycle`: 5 passed.
- `script_grblhal`: 11 passed.
- `script_linuxcnc`: 11 passed.
- `script_tormach`: 11 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The trial merge diff against upstream/main passes the whitespace check.

I repeated all three old-post mutations. Each mutation temporarily restored one post from upstream/main. The Tormach, grblHAL, and LinuxCNC mutations each failed both G73 and G85 refusal tests. Each restore passed all seven tests. All mutated files were restored.

The trial merge changes only the five intended files. No golden file changes remain against current upstream/main. There are no moved golden lines to check. No UI files change, so screenshots are not required.

Requested before merge: none.

No controller simulation or machine run was done. The gate dry run selected a broad batch from the old branch base. I ran the relevant post suites listed above instead.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
